# Onboarding addendum: rulings made during execution

Record of the decisions taken while executing `2026-10-03-onboarding-addendum-plan.md` (spec: `2026-10-02-onboarding-design.md`). The plan, the five parts in `parts/` and the screens 46 to 57 contain every ruling below; the spec keeps the approved design and defers to the addendum where they differ; this file says why, and what each costs if it is wrong. Executed 3 October 2026.

## Developer approvals

- 3 Oct 2026: "write the plan, then execute it with the recommended method without asking again; deliver only the final result ready for GPT review".
- 3 Oct 2026: "make every ruling per the recommendation, do not ask". The three rulings a reviewer marked "product owner to confirm" (items 6, 7 and 8 below) are confirmed by it.

## Rulings that shaped the addendum text

| # | Ruling | Why | Cost if wrong |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Overdue delegated tasks escalate to the default owner, then to the executive's attention queue (EXE-02, P0); the PLT-10 morning digest (P1) carries the same line once enabled. | No P0 requirement may depend on a P1 feature. | One amendment row, if the product owner prefers to raise PLT-10 to P0. |
| 2 | A late approval point never lacks approvers: until a person is named, the people holding the starting pack's role approve (shown as default); a role nobody holds fails the publish check and the dry run. | Keeps the GOV-21 publish check intact. | None found. |
| 3 | The onboarding agent and MCP clients using the setup tool group write only into the Draft workspace and its onboarding session (BR-43); after launch a setup call that carries a source becomes a suggestion that a person accepts. | Matches the spec and MCP-06, MCP-07. | None found. |
| 4 | `get_setup_context` also returns the session's open questions; no new tool. | Smallest change that serves the bring-your-own-AI prompt pack. | One more tool later. |
| 5 | Provenance has seven statuses everywhere: read, assumed, default, confirmed, asked, delegated, conflicting. | BR-45, section 10 and the screen badges already treated "default" as a status. | One word in three places. |
| 6 | The executive's attention queue shows assumed values as one item per owner, with the number still to confirm; it also absorbs that owner's overdue tasks. | Keeps the approved behaviour without about 64 rows on launch day (BRD v4.3 asks for 5 to 8 executive signals). | Two sentences and one screen line. |
| 7 | Hands-on time is the time the main setup person has the onboarding session open, from the first framing screen to launch, reading included while open; paused or closed time is not counted (section 4.1, ONB-26). | The 30-minute headline must be measured the same way by everyone. | One definition bullet. |
| 8 | "Use this" on a value only the executive knows marks it confirmed, not assumed (ONB-12). | Otherwise the executive's own answers come back to her queue. | One clause in ONB-12 and one in section 10.3. |
| 9 | A project adopted as committed without an owner or a sponsor is not blocked: the gap becomes a delegated item and an attention item until the person is named; the CHR-17 amendment row says so (BR-01, CHR-14). | v4.3 makes both mandatory before commitment; adoption needed an explicit exception. | Phrase-level, if the product owner prefers blocking. |
| 10 | Correcting a value that a baseline from import has locked opens a change request with the correction and its source (BR-47). | One reading of BR-47 for finance owners after launch. | One sentence, if a one-time re-capture is preferred. |
| 11 | ONB-19's moment-of-need example is the first opening of deliverable process frameworks (deferred), not capacity (delegated at launch). | Section 10.2 delegates capacity and defers process frameworks. | One criterion. |
| 12 | The bring-your-own-AI prompt "answer open questions" means proposing the values with the setup tools. | No tool submits an answer; the setup tools carry the values. | One phrase. |
| 13 | D-32's reason: understanding unstructured input needs a language model; structured files with an unambiguous mapping are read without it. | The first wording contradicted the exact-parser design. | None found. |
| 14 | The setup tool group is available from Release 1A, ahead of the update and prepare tools D-30 holds until 1B, because it writes only into a Draft workspace and its session; the M05 amendment row states it. | Spec placement; the exception had to be explicit. | One row and one milestone line, if the product owner moves it to 1B. |
| 15 | The v4.3 journeys "Tenant onboarding" and "Workspace setup (WSP-14)" stay valid for manual setup; one sentence in section 13 says so; the amendment table keeps 20 rows. | The manual path survives as the fallback. | One row later. |
| 16 | The routing of big or strategic projects uses GOV-06, which v4.3 places at 1B, so the dry run of ONB-14 completes at 1B. | Milestone placement must match v4.3. | One clause. |
| 17 | D-18 (SSO and email only in the MVP) gains the LLM provider and the vision service as P0 integrations for onboarding when the tenant enables the AI. | Stated in the Integrations amendment row instead of contradicting D-18 silently. | One clause. |
| 18 | Appendix D lists every market claim parts 01 and 03 rely on, each traced to a research-note line; the monday magic row has no Unverified mark because one note read the article through the Help Center API with timestamps (the cell says the other note could not open it). | The GPT reviewer checks claims against Appendix D. | One mark to add. |
| 19 | The 72% figure is about three-step tours completed, not users; the fields-versus-steps finding is about checkout flows. | Matches the studies. | None found. |

## Tooling

- `brd/source/build.py`: one build for two documents (`main`, `addendum-onboarding`); the main build ignores screens that cite ONB requirements, so BRD v4.3 stays byte-identical (verified after every change); the TOC page check folds curly quotes and the ellipsis to ASCII before comparing, because pandoc writes "Metis's" with a curly apostrophe; a missing anchor exits with a named error; the addendum summary omits the legacy mapping count.

## Process

- No git (the folder is not a repository and commits are manual): every review read a snapshot diff.
- Verbatim content was extracted from the plan by script, never retyped; every part stays byte-identical to its plan block.
- Implementers ran in parallel only on disjoint files; the controller alone edited the plan.
- The separate GPT review pack (plan Task 15) was skipped: the parallel session metis-f6 builds one combined pack (round 3: BRD v4.4, this addendum, all 58 wireframes) and does the v4.4 bump and the base switch inside this addendum after this plan's done message.

## Parked, with reasons (from the final review triage)

- House styling shared with all 58 screens: placeholder grey `--faint` (2.6:1, documented as placeholders only), the wireframe strip (4.4:1), compact table text, the empty project tree and demo counters of the app shell. A change would alter BRD v4.3 screens.
- Data the sample does not hold: per-finding source files in the Portfolio X-ray (adding them would invent data).
- Settled in the API design, not in the BRD: tool names, scopes and the agent token lifetime.
- P1 details: ONB-28 voice limit, ONB-34 pre-boarding reading rule, ONB-38 specialist cannot launch.
- Spec-approved and expected as GPT comments, not defects: the density of the first screen, the 30-minute target as a median, role grants at launch from AI-proposed roles in one approval, no complexity indicators for the 27 new P0 requirements, data-protection duties beyond EU AI Act Article 50.
- Cosmetic: the Word TOC entry for 11.3 keeps a straight apostrophe (Word rebuilds the field on open), "Project Online" wraps across lines in one PNG, one annotation marker sits beside its card.
